title: Failover, Switchover & Split-Brain Prevention
description: Understand planned switchovers, unplanned disaster failover, and quorum consensus to prevent Split-Brain scenarios.

data.text: In database clustering, **Switchover** is a controlled, planned promotion of a replica to primary (e.g. for maintenance). **Failover** is an emergency, automated promotion when the primary node crashes.

A **Split-Brain** occurs when a network partition disconnects nodes, causing both the old primary and the promoted replica to believe they are the authoritative primary. Both accept conflicting writes, causing irreversible data divergence. High-availability clusters prevent this using distributed consensus engines (etcd, Consul, Raft) with odd-numbered quorums (3 or 5 nodes).

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Switchovers are planned and safe; failovers are automated responses to disasters.
Prevent split-brain by requiring quorum consensus (3+ nodes) via etcd or Consul.
Fence old primaries using STONITH (Shoot The Other Node In The Head) or node termination.
